text:
Sean Gallagher: posting a Q&A thread here after today’s announcement on tiered SLOs + the error budget policy. ask anything — what changes for your team, where to see dashboards, release gates, overrides, etc.

Links:
• Tiered SLO definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGSRE/Tiered+SLO+Definitions+-+Hosted+vs+Dedicated
• Error budget policy + enforcement: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGSRE/Error+Budget+Policy+and+Enforcement
• Burn-rate alerting standard (for service owners): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ARCH/Error+Budget+Burn+Rate+Alerting+Standard
• Dashboard structure/naming: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/SLO+Dashboards+-+Structure+and+Naming

(reactions: :eyes: 21 :thumbsup: 34)


Dev Patel: for non-infra teams: what do we actually have to DO now? is this just SRE dashboards or are there new requirements for feature teams?

Rafael Mendes: good q. immediate change is mostly visibility + how we respond when budgets are burning.
- Everyone: if you own a production service in the request path (gateway/routing/runtime/console), your oncall will see burn-rate alerts + budget status.
- Service owners: add SLO dashboard link + runbook link in your service README/oncall docs (we’ll help w/ templates).
- Releases: we’re starting warn-only gates in CI for a pilot set. you’ll see a “budget risk” check but it won’t block yet.

Aisha Bello: + if you ship changes that affect request success/latency, you’ll start seeing canary analysis include “budget burn context” (e.g., ‘budget is already at 60% consumed in 7d window’). this is to avoid “death by a thousand cuts” during a shaky week.


Caleb Johnson: where are the dashboards? i clicked around Grafana and got lost.

Sergio Costa: in Grafana: folder is `SLOs / Tiered (Hosted + Dedicated)`.
Naming pattern: `SLO - <Tier> - <Service> - <Region>`.
Example: `SLO - Hosted - API Gateway - us-east`.
If you don’t see it, it’s likely permissions. ping #eng-observability or file INT ticket.

Nora Ahmed: we’re also linking dashboards from Console (internal) in the next MVP. but Grafana is source-of-truth for now.


Marissa Cole: for PMs: does this change what we promise customers? (esp Dedicated)

Lauren Bishop: no contract changes as part of this project (that’s separate). but yes, we now have clearer internal “what we aim for” by tier, and we’ll use it to drive comms + escalations. for Dedicated, the big difference is we’re measuring pool readiness + isolation-specific indicators (not just API 200s).

Sean Gallagher: + Dedicated messaging will be aligned w/ Support so we don’t end up with “SLA-ish” language in ad hoc emails. there’s a comms guideline doc coming.

Dev Patel: that’s helpful. do we have “what to say” when someone asks “are you within SLO today”?

Elliot Price: draft is here (still iterating): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/Error+Budget+Comms+Guidelines
TL;DR we communicate “customer impact + mitigation” vs “we burned 18% of budget”. the budget is mainly internal control + leading indicator.


Sahana Iyer: question on release gates: who gets blocked + when? I saw something in a pipeline today.

Connor O'Brien: current state:
- Pilot services only (gateway, routing policy engine, control plane pieces). Everyone else: no gating unless you opt in.
- Mode: WARN-ONLY until we announce date to move pilot to SOFT-BLOCK.
- SOFT-BLOCK means: default block on progression, but override available w/ approval.
- HARD-BLOCK is later + only after we’ve tuned false positives.

Aisha Bello: if you saw it today, it’s likely the check posting a comment like “Budget status: OK / At Risk / Exhausted” with a link to the budget view.


Jordan Lee: how do we request an override? is it a ticket? slack? some token?

Connor O'Brien: overrides are explicit + time-bound.
Process (for pilot):
1) request in #eng-sre (tag @oncall-sre) + include: service, tier, region, rollout link, why needed, mitigation/rollback plan.
2) SRE oncall (or SRE manager) issues an override token with TTL (default 2h) recorded in audit log.
3) pipeline step reads token and continues.
Doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Release+Gates+Using+Error+Budgets

Rafael Mendes: and we’ll say “no” sometimes. the point is to force a deliberate tradeoff when the system is already unhealthy.


Amara Diallo: does this affect how we count 499s / client aborts? I remember we had confusion there.

Aisha Bello: yep — part of the standardization. we now classify streaming disconnects into:
- client abort (usually not charged as failure unless we see server-side signal)
- server disconnect (counts against availability)
- timeout bucketed separately (gateway vs upstream)
Spec is here: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGSRE/SLI+Spec+-+Success%2C+Timeouts%2C+Streaming+Disconnects

Sean Gallagher: and we’ve already had one hotfix where we were overcounting 499-ish behavior, so please keep reporting mismatches.


Chloe Martin: for Console: what are we showing and when? people are asking for “error budget remaining” in UI.

Marissa Cole: MVP scope:
- “Budget remaining” + burn rate trend per tier + region, with change history overlay (deploy markers)
- links out to canonical dashboards
- rollout integration: show gate status + reason + override audit link
Timeline is phased; we’ll keep using Grafana + CI comments until then.

Nikhil Sharma: will Hosted tier have different targets by model? or is it just one global number?

Rafael Mendes: targets are tier-specific and SLI-specific. within a tier, we’re measuring by route/service/region and (where cardinality permits) by model family.
We’re not doing “every model gets its own contract-like SLO” right now because it explodes metrics + makes oncall impossible. Instead:
- hosted: primary SLOs at API surface + critical internal services
- model-specific views exist for debugging/optimization, but policy decisions are tier/service based initially

Allison Grant: + we’re enforcing cardinality budgets. please don’t add new labels like `prompt_hash` or customer IDs to SLO metrics.
If you need high-cardinality debugging, use logs/traces.


Neha Kapoor: adding exec note: please treat this as a behavior change, not a reporting exercise. when budgets burn, we slow down changes and bias toward mitigation + stability. the goal is fewer 2am incidents + fewer “why did latency regress” surprises.


Miles Thornton: quick pointer on “what to do when budget is near/exhausted” (for oncall): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/Error+Budget+Exhaustion+Response+Runbook
Top mitigations we expect teams to try (in order):
1) rollback recent change / disable risky flags
2) fallback routing (compatible model variant / region failover) where allowed
3) protective throttling for Hosted to stop cascading failure

Dev Patel: does protective throttling mean customers get 429s?

Miles Thornton: can, yes. but it’s controlled + better than prolonged 5xx/timeout storms. comms guidelines call out how we message that (and Dedicated is handled differently — we don’t want to violate isolation/capacity commitments).


incident-bot: Reminder: if you’re seeing a live reliability issue, use #incidents and follow the incident process. This thread is for Q&A only.

Caleb Johnson: last one: what about Private deployments?

Sean Gallagher: Private is partial scope. we’ll publish mapping guidance (what SLOs *would* correspond to) but we’re not enforcing gates there initially since customers operate the environment. If you’re working on Private, we still want you to instrument SLIs the same way so teams can reason consistently.

Aisha Bello: if you’re a Private owner and want to opt into internal budget tracking (for your own ops), ping us — we can set it up without “blocking” anything.


Sergio Costa: if anyone notices missing dashboards for your service, drop a note w/ service name + region and we’ll queue it. we’re still filling in some gaps.

Sean Gallagher: keep the questions coming. if it’s service-specific, best channel is #eng-sre / #eng-observability, but we’ll monitor here too.
